title: Kevin Feige recalls Patrick Stewart spoiling Star Trek: Picard on the Doctor Strange set
body_md:
*November 27, 2026*

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige has shared an amusing memory of working with Patrick Stewart during the production of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, Feige recalled that his conversations with the actor occasionally ventured into an entirely different fictional universe. Rather than discussing confidential Marvel storylines, Stewart was revealing details about Star Trek: Picard, a television series Feige was eager to experience without advance knowledge.

## The Marvel chief wanted to avoid spoilers

As a Star Trek enthusiast, Feige might seem like the ideal person to ask Stewart questions about the series. According to his recollection, however, he did not need to solicit any information. Stewart offered some plot details of his own accord, prompting Feige to ask him to stop. He wanted to enjoy the show as a regular viewer instead of discovering its surprises through conversations at work.

The situation is particularly entertaining given Marvel Studios' reputation for protecting the secrets of its upcoming films. Much of the public conversation around Marvel productions revolves around avoiding leaks and preserving major surprises. Here, the person concerned about hearing too much was the studio president himself, and the production whose secrets he wanted to preserve was not even a Marvel project.

Feige's account does not identify the particular developments Stewart disclosed, leaving audiences free to appreciate the anecdote without learning any of the show's twists.

## Two celebrated screen identities

Stewart occupies a distinctive position in popular culture because of his association with both Jean-Luc Picard and Charles Xavier. His appearances as Picard established an enduring connection with science fiction audiences, while the X-Men films introduced his interpretation of Professor X to generations of superhero fans.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness brought a version of Xavier into the Marvel Cinematic Universe in 2022. The encounter between Feige and Stewart therefore represented more than an ordinary conversation between a producer and an actor: it brought together people whose professional lives intersect with several decades of genre entertainment.

With Avengers: Doomsday scheduled for December 18, 2026, interest in the relationship between the X-Men and the wider Marvel universe has intensified again. The report connects Stewart with Xavier's return, although Feige's anecdote offers no new information about the character's role or the upcoming film's plot.

Ultimately, the charm of this story lies in its familiarity. Even a producer responsible for enormous cinematic franchises can experience the same excitement and apprehension as any other television fan when someone threatens to reveal what happens next.
